Over 400m, David Bailey in only his third attempt at the distance including the heats, set up a worthy personal best of 58.6 and was unlucky not to get amongst the medals, coming through strongly in the finishing straight.
Front Page: David Bailey strides out to win the Senior Boys 100m at the Club Championships and shows fine style in the process. Ivan Beaumont was second and Mark Shippen third.
As shown on this issue's cover, David Bailey led home the field in the senior boys' sprint with some hot opposition breathing down his neck.

Richard Danpure spearheaded our 14 - 16 team which really consisted of shorter distance track men. Unfortunately David Bailey became ill immediately after the race but we are glad to report that he soon fully recovered.
Youngsters David Bailey and Ivan Beaumont continued their sprinting rivalry and in spite of running in 'A' and 'B' strings both clocked almost identical times.

He now rates as Belgrave's regular number one with the spear, and has a best of 53.31 metres set in a school match where he also had the galling experience of throwing 59.52 metres only to have it doubtfully ruled an invalid throw. Other personal bests were set by David Bailey and Martin Munroe - both over 400m.

Once again both competitions were really close with only three points covering Youths Paul Churchley, Richard Danpure and Dave Bailey, and two points separating the first two Boys John Fernee and Philippe Weldin.
Coaching Course, amongst them seven Belgravians:- Stephen Sampson, Richard Danpure, Peter Crosbie, Paul Churchley, David Bailey, Peter Gardner and myself.
There were two double victors amongst the juniors with the 100/200 going to Dave Bailey and Adrian Cook taking the 1,500m. and retaining the 800m.

Left: Anna Matthews (8) and Diane Cook (1) competed in the Senior Ladies 3,000 metre walk at the Club Championships. Right: Junior David Bailey had good cause to smile after collecting his haul of trophies at the end of the meeting.
Young David Bailey who seems to have been around for years but is still only a first year junior impressed all with his very relaxed 4 x 400 relay run, coming on strong at the end of his lap.
Nice running came from another of our youngsters Dave Bailey. His 400 metres showed just a hint of what this boy could be capable of with regular training.

Our younger members made their presence felt on both field and the track with Matt King picking up 6 points in the heavy events, Mark Shippen beating all other competitors in the pole vault by nearly half a metre, and an inspired Dave Bailey cut his best 400 metres down to 52.8 and then ran 51.6 in the relay.
Dave Bailey put up another good performance in the one lap sprint and John Gladwin, a youth, came very close to the Club Record in the 800 metres.
Teams: 1.Aldershot F & D 191; 2.Shaftesbury H 253; 3.Invicta 258; 33.Belgrave H 1649; 54 teams closed in. Dave Bailey placed 172nd in the Junior race with Brian Marmion, on this occasion, a dnf'er.
Clive Holmes took the Junior Club Championship over 5 miles in 32:23 with Mark Waller 2nd 34:41, Brian Marmion 3rd 35:21 and David Bailey 4th 38:17.
